system_prompt_style.note: StateM is a CLI runbook driven by a host agent (Codex, Claude Code). The host builds the system prompt, and the bundle contains no prompt-assembly code. Per-node prompts are served via `statem cur`.

env_context_strategy.note: Repository context is supplied by the host agent. No StateM source is in the evidence.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: `statem compact-prompt` for safe compaction inside cyclic runbooks;
context_compaction.note: StateM only generates compaction/resume prompts. The actual compaction is done by the host.

observation_format.note: The CLI emits text and `--json`, but observation formatting to the model belongs to the host.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: StateM's core remains host-agnostic: any agent that can run shell commands can query and advance a runbook.
tool_call_format.note: The agent drives StateM through `statem` CLI commands with flags. Host tool-call syntax is not in the evidence.

tool_count.note: StateM does not define model tools; the host agent supplies them.

edit_primitive.note: No edit tool in StateM; editing is handled by the host.

protocol_standardization.note: Source code was not included in the evidence, so no grep was possible. Codex/Claude plugin packaging is present.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: It keeps planning, execution, verification, repair, and handoff from collapsing into one long prompt.
loop_primitives.note: The runbook graph (prepare -> execute -> verify -> handoff, plus a repair loop) is user-authored. The inner react loop belongs to the host.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: StateM moves that procedural state out of the model context and into a lightweight, versioned runbook.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: StateM's core remains host-agnostic: any agent that can run shell commands can query and advance a runbook.
multi_agent_topology.note: An optional isolated router is mentioned in the verification guide. Dynamic checks record `--agent-id`.

human_in_loop.note: The `manual` check type gates state transitions. on_completion is the closest value; this gating is opt-in per runbook.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: persist the current node, transitions, hook results, evidence, timestamps, and spec identity.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: Keep large outputs and durable decisions in files; keep the active model context focused on the current state.
long_term_memory.note: Also relevant: the `STATEM_STATE_DIR` durable state, and the Codex skill packaging.

state_persistence.note: Also relevant: `statem prompt` generates a post-clear resume prompt.

self_verification.evidence_quote: Delegate a structured review to an external command/model
self_verification.note: `command` gates run tests before a transition. Bounded self-review is described in docs/verification-guide.md. All of these are runbook-configured.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: If a blocking check fails, the agent remains in the current state with the failure recorded for repair.
retry_policy.note: This is a state-level repair loop rather than whole-task retries.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: It allows the host to stop when no active run exists, the current state is terminal, or the graph has no outgoing transition.
termination_condition.note: Reaching a terminal node requires passing gates. Step and cost caps belong to the host.

timeouts.evidence_quote: Checks can be configured with fields such as `blocking`, `on_failure`, `timeout`, and `cwd`.

execution_isolation.note: Execution happens in the host environment. Harbor/Terminal-Bench containers are used in the evaluations.

permission_model.note: The gates apply to state transitions, not to individual actions.

eval_hooks.note: Evidence: the Harbor adapters in integrations/harbor/.

target_domain.evidence_quote: A command-line state machine for reliable, long-running AI agents.
target_domain.note: The examples are coding and terminal tasks (Terminal-Bench).

open_source.evidence_quote: StateM is released under the [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE).

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: StateM's core remains host-agnostic: any agent that can run shell commands can query and advance a runbook.

primary_artifact.evidence_quote: CLI runbook for agent long run.
